title: Rooting Media, Moisture, and Oxygen
objective: Relate rooting-medium physical properties to water supply, gas exchange, temperature, and root development.

terms.definition: The fraction of substrate pore volume filled with air at a defined moisture or drainage state.
The amount of water a substrate retains under a defined measurement condition; the value is method- and container-dependent.
Dry substrate mass per unit bulk volume, including pore space.
Physical contact that permits water movement between the rooting medium and cutting base.
A moisture state in which most or all connected pore space is filled with water.
A discrete propagation substrate unit used to support a cutting during root initiation and early establishment.

coreScience: An unrooted cutting needs continuous water contact at the base, but living tissue also needs oxygen. A medium that remains saturated can restrict gas exchange, while a medium that dries or shrinks away from the stem can interrupt hydraulic contact.

Rooting media differ in pore size, water retention, drainage, sterility status, structural stability, and chemistry. In a study of eight high-CBD hemp cultivars, medium had a large effect on rooting and rockwool performed best among the tested treatments. That result is evidence for those cultivars and methods, not proof that rockwool is universally superior.
Container geometry, plug compression, insertion depth, irrigation method, temperature, and rooting density change the actual air-water environment. Media must be evaluated as installed systems.
cultivationRelevance: Standardize media batch, plug preparation, saturation method, drainage, insertion depth, tray position, and irrigation. Avoid comparing hormone treatments across uncontrolled media conditions.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Medium composition and lot; plug dimensions; pre-wet method; water content or mass; drainage; temperature; EC/pH context; rooting and transplant outcomes.

misconceptions: One media brand works the same in every tray and cultivar.
Rockwool is proven best for all cannabis propagation.
evidenceLimits: Media results are genotype- and system-specific. Physical measurements are more transferable than brand claims.
